newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai Danu to take over, not merge with Fin One.
newsitem.headline: Thai Danu to take over, not merge with Fin One.

text.p: Thai Danu Bank Plc plans to take over Finance One Plc rather than merge with the company, central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Tuesday.
"They have changed from merger to acquisition because their earlier plans of merging company A with company B had run into a relatively large number of problems," he told reporters.
Last week Thai Danu Bank denied rumours it had decided to take over cash-strapped Finance One instead of merging with the company that was once Thailand's largest finance firm.

The bank said on Friday the due diligence process had gone too far to switch from the merger. Boards of directors of both companies were due to hold meetings on Thursday to vote on the merger once due diligence was completed.
Rergnchai did not say what the deadline for the takeover was, but said: "We have given them a timeframe and they should come up with some progress by next week.
Central bank officials were quoted by local media last week as saying the central bank preferred a takeover to a merger if it could speed up the rescue of Finance One.
The comments came on the heels of rumours that Thai Danu was planning to walk away from the merger due to various problems.

Analysts said due diligence likely exposed Finance One's weak financial position. They had said earlier Thai Danu's shareholders were not expected to approve a merger once the extent of Finance One's problems were known.

Analysts say Finance One sought the merger -- which would have been the largest between two Thai financial institutions -- because it faced liquidity problems that emerged during a major shakeup of Thailand's troubled finance sector.
Rergnchai told a seminar on future mergers of finance companies that the government would give generous incentives to finance companies that planned to merge.
The incentives would allow the finance firms to do foreign exchange business and retail banking. Most finance companies are currently not licenced to undertake these businesses.
"This is a golden opportunity for finance companies to merge," Rergnchai said. "They can choose either to be big department stores or remain as small boutique shops."
The Thai government has urged finance companies to merge as part of an effort to stabilise the sector, which has been heavily exposed to the troubled property sector.
